words: word; letter; sentence; space; page; top; bottom; left; right; first; last
notes: Print concepts, taught in the first weeks and revisited while they are needed: follow print left to right, top to bottom and page by page with a finger under each word (RF.K.1a); know that a spoken word is written as a set sequence of letters, and count the words in a sentence, pointing to the first and the last (RF.K.1b); point to each word of a memorized line, using the spaces to find where a word ends (RF.K.1c). Practised on large-print shared texts: a short class poem or chant of 4 to 8 lines, the module's big-book read-aloud, and the class's own dictated sentences. First grade of the band: nothing comes before, and the standard has no prompting clause, so by the end of the year the child tracks alone. Boundary: finger-pointing is matched to spoken words, not to syllables; the RF.K.1 parent is completed on ek-letter-names (letter names).

words: letter; uppercase; lowercase; capital; alphabet; name
notes: Recognize and name all 26 uppercase and lowercase letters, in isolation and inside a text (RF.K.1d, which completes RF.K.1), and print many of them with correct formation (L.K.1a, here because letter names and letter formation are taught together in the base text's daily letter routine). The base text introduces two or three letters a cycle across the first two modules (a and t first, then h, p, n, c, m, r, v, s, g, i, d, f, l, k, y, q, u, x, b, o, w, j, e, z), each with its sound (ek-letter-sounds) and a formation chant. Practised on alphabet charts, letter cards, the class poem and names of classmates. First grade of the band; the demand is all letters named by the end of kindergarten, but only 'many' printed (grade 1 asks for all, L.1.1a). Boundary: no cursive; formation taught with top-to-bottom strokes on lined paper.

words: rhyme; beat; syllable; clap; blend; break apart; beginning sound; ending chunk
notes: Phonological awareness with larger sound units, spoken only, before phonemes: hear and make rhymes, pick the word that does not rhyme, and change an onset to make a new rhyme (RF.K.2a); count, say, blend and break apart syllables in spoken words, clapping the beats (RF.K.2b); blend and split onset and rime in single-syllable words, first copying the teacher and then alone in CVC words (RF.K.2c). Order follows the base text: rhyme and syllables in module 1, onset and rime in modules 2 and 3. Practised on oral games, nursery-style rhymes and chants, and names of the module's topic words (toy, weather words). First grade of the band. Boundary: no print is needed; this is listening and speaking work, about 5 to 10 minutes a day.

words: sound; first sound; middle sound; last sound; blend; segment; change
notes: Phonemic awareness in three-sound (CVC) spoken words: isolate and say the first, the middle vowel and the last sound (RF.K.2d); blend three spoken sounds into a word and segment a word into its sounds, then add or change one sound to make a new word (mat to sat, sat to sit, sit to sip) (RF.K.2e, which completes RF.K.2). Taught after ek-early-phonology, from module 2 on, with a daily blending and segmentation routine using fingers or sound boxes. Practised orally on words that will soon be decoded in print. First grade of the band. Boundary, from the standard: CVC words ending in /l/, /r/ or /x/ are left out; no blends or digraphs are segmented in kindergarten.

words: sound; letter; consonant; vowel; short vowel; sh; ch; th
notes: Letter-sound correspondences: say the primary sound of every consonant (RF.K.3a) and the short sound of each vowel, and write the letter or letters for most consonant and short-vowel sounds heard (L.K.2c, spelling, here because it is the same map run the other way). Order follows the base text's letter order (a, t, h, p, n, c, m, r ... e, z) over modules 1 and 2, then the digraphs sh, th and ch at the start of module 3. Introduces the sound-spelling-map: a wall chart of sounds with the letters that spell them, added to as each correspondence is taught, used for reading and for spelling. Practised on letter cards, picture-sound sorts and dictation of single sounds. First grade of the band. Boundary: one main sound per letter; alternate spellings wait for grade 1. Never taught as 'guess from the picture': a keyword picture only helps recall the sound.

words: blend; read; spell; short a; short i; short u; short o; short e; long vowel; vowel name; chain
notes: Blending and decoding begin in module 3: read and spell CVC words with short a, then i, u, o and e (one vowel a cycle, as the base text orders them), then words with the digraphs sh, ch, th, word families -an and -am, -ank and -ink, and double final consonants (moss) in module 4 (RF.K.3, completed here). RF.K.3b: associate each of the five vowel letters with its short sound (decoded) and its long sound (the letter's name, heard in spoken words; the base text brings long vowels in spoken words only in the last cycles). RF.K.3d: chaining, change one letter (pin to pen, hot to not) and say which sound changed. L.K.2d: spell simple words phonetically from the sound-spelling-map. Practised on word chains, dictation and the decodable texts of ek-emergent-reader. First grade of the band. Boundary: CVCe and vowel teams are not decoded until grade 1.

words: the; of; to; you; she; my; is; are; do; does; a; I; see; we
notes: Read common high-frequency words by sight, in a list and in a text (RF.K.3c), two or three a cycle across the year (the standard's examples: the, of, to, you, she, my, is, are, do, does). Each word is taught by mapping it: say it, tap its sounds, mark the letters that spell their sounds regularly and the part to learn by heart, then read it in a sentence. Practised in the class poem, sentence strips and the decodable texts. First grade of the band. Boundary: a word is read from its letters, never guessed from a picture or the first letter; the word list is kept in step with the decodable texts.

words: read; reread; book; decodable; enjoy; learn
notes: Read emergent-reader texts with purpose and understanding (RF.K.4): from module 3 on, short decodable texts (about 20 to 80 words, one sentence a page) written only with the letter-sounds and high-frequency words already taught, read with a partner, reread, and talked about (what happened, what did you learn). Curio Class writes its own decodable texts, each checked against the sound-spelling-map and word list taught to that cycle; some are on the module's topic (trees, weather) so decoding and knowledge meet. The base text teaches this through small-group conferring and partner reading rather than a set lesson, so the scope and sequence plans it as a daily small-group routine. First grade of the band. Boundary: no levelled 'predictable' books that rely on picture cues; the child reads every word from its letters.

words: question; answer; who; what; where; when; detail; I heard
notes: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a story (RL.K.1) and in an informational text (RI.K.1), and, during and after a read-aloud, confirm understanding by asking and answering about key details and asking for help when something is not understood (SL.K.2, the listening side of the same skill). Practised on the module's read-alouds: picture books and short informational texts read aloud, well above what a kindergartner can decode (the base text: about two or three grade levels above independent level), on the year's topic sets: toys and play, weather, trees as living things, people enjoying trees. Questions are text-dependent and go from what the text says to why. First grade of the band; 'with prompting and support' is the kindergarten wording that grade 1 removes. Boundary: answers point back to a page or a line heard, not to life experience alone.

words: listen; read along; join in; reread; chant
notes: Actively engage in group reading of stories, poems and informational texts with purpose and understanding (RL.K.10 for literature, RI.K.10 for informational, the same skill on two kinds of text). Shared reading of big books and class poems: students chime in, read the parts they can, and reread the same text over several days for a new purpose each time. Texts: the module's read-alouds and a weekly shared poem on the topic. The reading volume is mostly heard text in kindergarten; the read-aloud is complex text, the shared poem is short and patterned. First grade of the band; grade 1 asks the child to read grade 1 prose and poetry with prompting and support (RL.1.10, RI.1.10), so the move is from joining in to reading. Boundary: engagement is shown by talk and joining in, not by a reading level.

words: retell; beginning; middle; end; first; next; then; last
notes: With prompting and support, retell a familiar story, including key details, in order (RL.K.2), using picture cards and the story-map (who, where, what happened first, next, last). Practised on picture-book read-alouds heard several times, such as stories about playing with toys or a character facing a storm. Retelling is oral and drawn; a few labels or words may be dictated. First grade of the band; grade 1 adds the central message or lesson (RL.1.2). Boundary: retelling is the story's events in order, not a personal reaction.

words: character; setting; event; problem; story
notes: With prompting and support, identify the characters, the setting and the major events of a story (RL.K.3). Introduces the story-map: a simple chart (characters, setting, events) filled in by drawing and dictation. Practised on picture-book read-alouds in each module, for example a weather story where a character is caught in a storm (module 2). First grade of the band; grade 1 asks the child to describe them using key details (RL.1.3). Boundary: identify and name, not yet describe or explain.

words: word; meaning; means; another meaning; ending; -s; -ed; -ing; un-; re-
notes: Ask and answer questions about unknown words in a story (RL.K.4) and, with prompting and support, in an informational text (RI.K.4); learn a new meaning for a familiar word (duck the bird and to duck) (L.K.4a); use the most common endings and affixes (-s, -ed, -ing, re-, un-, -ful, -less) as a clue to meaning (L.K.4b, which completes L.K.4). Introduces word-parts: a word can be a base plus an ending or prefix that changes its meaning. Practised on words from the read-alouds (weather words, tree words) and the class word wall. First grade of the band; grade 1 adds sentence-level context and root words (L.1.4). Boundary: this is word meaning; decoding is never replaced by guessing from the picture.

words: storybook; poem; information book; cover; back cover; title page; title; author; illustrator
notes: Know books: recognize common kinds of text, storybooks and poems (RL.K.5); name the front cover, back cover and title page (RI.K.5); name the author and illustrator and say what each does, for a story (RL.K.6, with prompting and support) and for an informational text (RI.K.6). The four codes are one book-handling routine taught at the start of each read-aloud in module 1 and repeated. Practised on every module's read-alouds, Curio Class picture books and poems with their own credits. First grade of the band; grade 1 asks the child to tell books that tell stories from books that give information (RL.1.5) and to use text features to find facts (RI.1.5). Boundary: kinds of text are stories, poems and information books only.

words: picture; illustration; photograph; shows; page; moment
notes: With prompting and support, describe how an illustration relates to the words: what moment of a story a picture shows (RL.K.7) and what person, place, thing or idea in an informational text a picture or photograph shows (RI.K.7). Practised on picture-book read-alouds and photographs in informational texts on toys, weather and trees. First grade of the band; grade 1 uses illustrations and details to describe characters, setting and events (RL.1.7) and key ideas (RI.1.7). Boundary: the picture is matched to words already heard; the question is never answerable from the picture alone, and pictures are never used to guess a printed word.

words: same; different; both; compare; alike
notes: With prompting and support, compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in familiar stories (RL.K.9), and name basic likenesses and differences between two texts on the same topic, in pictures, descriptions or steps (RI.K.9). One compare-two routine on two kinds of text: a two-column chart, then 'Both ... ; but ...'. Practised in module 4 on two stories of characters who care for a tree, and in module 3 on two informational texts about trees. First grade of the band; grade 1 drops 'with prompting and support' (RL.1.9, RI.1.9). Boundary: both texts are familiar from earlier read-alouds.

words: topic; about; detail; fact; teaches
cross_subject: science:K-ESS2-1 (weather texts read in the weather module carry the patterns science records)
notes: With prompting and support, name the main topic of an informational text and retell its key details (RI.K.2). Introduces main-idea-details: a topic box with detail boxes under it. Practised on short informational read-alouds (a few hundred words) on weather, trees and living things, often reread. First grade of the band; grade 1 asks the same without prompting (RI.1.2), and grade 2 the topic of a multiparagraph text and of each paragraph (RI.2.2). Boundary: topic, not yet main idea as a sentence.

words: connect; because; so; first; next; then; same
notes: With prompting and support, describe the connection between two people, events, ideas or pieces of information in a text (RI.K.3): what happens first and next, what causes what (a tree needs water, so its roots grow toward it). Introduces text-structure in its simplest form: order and because. Practised on informational read-alouds on weather and living things; the base text assesses it in the trees module. First grade of the band; grade 1 removes the prompting (RI.1.3), grade 2 asks for a series of events, ideas or steps (RI.2.3). Boundary: two pieces of information at a time.

words: reason; point; why; because; author thinks
notes: With prompting and support, identify the reasons an author gives to support a point (RI.K.8): 'The author says trees are important. One reason is ...'. Introduces claim-evidence-reasoning in its kindergarten form: a point with its reasons, drawn as a box with arrows. Practised on a short informational text that states a point (why trees matter to a community, module 4). First grade of the band; grade 1 removes the prompting (RI.1.8). Boundary: reasons are stated in the text; the child does not judge them.

words: opinion; favorite; I like; I think; best
notes: Use drawing, dictating and writing to name a topic or book and state an opinion or preference about it (W.K.1): 'My favorite toy is ...', 'I would plant a tree at ...'. Taught with a modelled piece, then a shared one, then the child's own. Practised on the module topics: toys (module 1) and where to plant a tree (module 4, the base text's opinion unit). First grade of the band; the kindergarten standard asks only topic and opinion; grade 1 adds a reason and closure (W.1.1). The child may add 'because' orally; it is not required. Boundary: writing is a drawing with a sentence, words spelled phonetically.

words: teach; fact; label; topic; about
cross_subject: science:K-LS1-1 (writing about what trees and animals need)
notes: Use drawing, dictating and writing to name a topic and give some information about it (W.K.2): a labelled drawing and a sentence or two about a classmate's toy (module 1), a weather fact, a tree and what lives on it (module 3). Taught from a model piece built with the class. Writing draws on the read-alouds and observations. First grade of the band; grade 1 adds 'some facts' and a sense of closure (W.1.2). Boundary: the piece names the topic and supplies information; no structure beyond that is required.

words: story; first; next; then; at the end; I felt
notes: Use drawing, dictating and writing to narrate a single event or a few loosely linked events, in the order they happened, with a reaction (W.K.3). Introduces narrative-arc: a three-box first, next, last plan, with a feeling at the end. Practised on a weather story about a character caught in weather, after reading weather stories (module 2, the base text's narrative performance task). First grade of the band; grade 1 asks for two or more sequenced events, details, time words and closure (W.1.3). Boundary: events may be loosely linked; drawing carries much of the story.

words: draft; share; add; detail; question; publish
notes: With help from adults, answer a partner's questions and suggestions and add details to a drawing or a piece of writing (W.K.5), and explore digital tools to make and publish writing, with peers (W.K.6). Introduces writing-process in its kindergarten form: draft, share, add, publish. Practised on the module performance tasks (the toy piece, the weather story, the tree collage, the tree card). First grade of the band; grade 1 adds 'focus on a topic' (W.1.5). Teacher note: a class without devices publishes on paper and records with a teacher-held device; no child accounts are made, and no child's name or photograph is posted outside the class.

words: question; find out; research; notebook; observe; record
cross_subject: science:K-LS1-1 (research on what trees and animals need)
notes: Take part in shared research and writing projects (W.K.7) and, with help, recall information from experience or gather it from provided sources to answer a question (W.K.8). Introduces research-cycle in its kindergarten form: a class question, look and listen in two or three provided texts and observations, record in a drawing notebook, share. Practised in the weather journal (module 2) and the research notebook on trees and what depends on them (module 3, the base text's research module). First grade of the band; grade 1 keeps the same wording, so the growth is in the kind of project (how-to books, birds). Boundary: sources are chosen by the teacher.

words: listen; take turns; partner; ask; answer; help; agree
notes: Take part in conversations with partners and groups about kindergarten topics and texts: follow agreed rules (listen, take turns) and keep a conversation going through several exchanges (SL.K.1); ask and answer questions to get help, get information or clear up what is not understood (SL.K.3). Introduces discussion-protocol: named routines (turn and talk, partner interview, a class circle, a science talk) with sentence starters that fade. Practised on the module texts and topics; the base text assesses a partner interview about a toy (module 1) and science talks about living things (module 3). First grade of the band; grade 1 adds building on others' talk (SL.1.1b) and asking questions to clear up confusion (SL.1.1c). Boundary: exchanges are short; the teacher models every routine first.

words: describe; tell; detail; drawing; speak up; clearly
notes: Describe familiar people, places, things and events, adding detail with prompting (SL.K.4); add drawings or other visuals to a description (SL.K.5); speak audibly and say thoughts, feelings and ideas clearly (SL.K.6). Practised by describing a toy, the day's weather or a tree the class visits, and in the end-of-module share. First grade of the band; grade 1 asks for relevant details and complete sentences (SL.1.4, SL.1.6). Teacher note: when children describe family or home, the teacher accepts any family, offers 'a person you know' as an alternative, and does not press for private details.

words: noun; action word; who; what; where; when; why; how; in; on; under; to; from
notes: Grammar used in speech and in shared writing: frequently occurring nouns and verbs (L.K.1b); regular plurals formed orally with /s/ or /es/ (dog, dogs; wish, wishes) (L.K.1c); question words who, what, where, when, why, how (L.K.1d); the most common prepositions (in, out, on, off, to, from, with) (L.K.1e). Taught through the read-aloud texts and oral sentence games, not as labels to memorize. First grade of the band; grade 1 adds common, proper and possessive nouns, pronouns, verb tense, adjectives, conjunctions and determiners (L.1.1). Boundary: parts of speech are used, not defined; the L.K.1 parent is completed on ek-sentences.

words: sentence; capital; period; question mark; exclamation mark; I
notes: Make and expand complete sentences in shared language work (L.K.1f, which completes L.K.1), and write them with a capital for the first word and for I (L.K.2a) and a named end mark (L.K.2b), which completes L.K.2 with the spelling work of ek-letter-sounds and ek-cvc-decoding. Introduces sentence-combining in its first form: expand a short sentence with who, where or how (The dog ran. The big dog ran to the park.). Practised in interactive sentence building on module topics (the base text moves from building to interactive writing in module 3). First grade of the band; grade 1 asks for simple and compound sentences of four kinds (L.1.1j) and more capitals and commas (L.1.2). Boundary: one or two sentences a piece.

words: sort; group; opposite; walk; march; tiptoe; stomp; colorful; word
notes: With adult help, explore how words relate (L.K.5): sort objects and pictures into categories (toys by how they move, weather by kind) (L.K.5a); pair common verbs and adjectives with their opposites (L.K.5b); find real-life uses of a word (places at school that are colorful) (L.K.5c); act out shades of meaning among verbs for the same action (walk, march, strut, prance) (L.K.5d). Use the words and phrases learned from talk and read-alouds (L.K.6). Practised on each module's word list, drawn from its texts, met before, during and after reading. First grade of the band; grade 1 sorts words (not objects), defines by category and attribute, and adds adjective intensity (L.1.5). Boundary: oral and acted, not written definitions.

words: sentence; capital letter; period; question mark; exclamation mark; first word
notes: Recognize the features of a sentence: its first word, the capital at the start, and the end punctuation (RF.1.1a, which is all of RF.1.1 in grade 1). Practised in decodable texts, interactive editing of class sentences, and finding sentences in the module read-aloud. Grows from kindergarten print concepts (word, space, first and last word, ek-print-concepts) and capital and end mark (ek-sentences) to the sentence as a unit read with expression at its end mark. Text: decodable texts of 2 to 6 sentences a page. Boundary: kinds of end mark are named, not the four sentence types (those are L.1.1j).

words: long vowel; short vowel; blend; segment; sound; consonant blend
notes: Phonemic awareness in single-syllable spoken words of four and five sounds: tell long from short vowel sounds (RF.1.2a); blend sounds into words, including consonant blends (st, fl, spl) (RF.1.2b); isolate first, middle vowel and last sounds (RF.1.2c); segment a word into its complete sequence of sounds (RF.1.2d). Daily, short, oral, and tied to the week's spelling pattern so each sound is mapped to its spelling on the sound-spelling-map. Grows from kindergarten's three-sound CVC words (ek-phonemes) to words with clusters and long vowels. Boundary: still spoken words; the printed side is e1-short-vowels and e1-long-vowels.

words: digraph; sh; ch; th; wh; ck; ng; nk; blend; cluster; short vowel
notes: Know the spellings of the common consonant digraphs (sh, ch, th, wh, ck, ng) (RF.1.3a) and decode regularly spelled one-syllable words (RF.1.3b): CVC, CCVC, CVCC and longer, with short a, i, u, then o (with j, w, x), then a long stay on short e (the base text gives it two cycles as the hardest to hear), then -ng and -nk, initial clusters with l and r, final clusters (-st, -nd, -lt), and the doubled final consonants -ll, -ss, -ff, -zz. Order follows the base text's grade 1 modules 1 and 2. Practised in word chains, dictation and decodable texts written only with patterns taught to date. Grows from kindergarten CVC words and three digraphs (ek-cvc-decoding). Boundary: one-syllable short-vowel words; long vowels are e1-long-vowels.

words: long vowel; silent e; vowel team; ai; ay; ea; ee; oa; ow; igh; ie; y; ar; or; er
notes: Know final -e and the common vowel teams for long vowel sounds (RF.1.3c): open syllables (he, go, my), then CVCe across all five vowels (a_e first, then i_e, o_e, u_e, e_e), then in the last module the teams ai, ay, ea, ee, oa, ow, -y, ie, igh, and oo. The base text also teaches r-controlled vowels (ar, or, er, ir, ur) in grade 1 module 4, ahead of the standards; they are kept here so grade 2 can review them. Practised in decodable texts that use only taught patterns, sentence dictation and spelling to complement reading. Grows from kindergarten, where long vowels were only the letter's name heard in speech (ek-cvc-decoding). Boundary: grade 1 learns the common teams; additional teams (oi, oy, ou, aw) are grade 2 (RF.2.3b).

words: syllable; vowel sound; closed; open; silent e; compound word; split
notes: Use the rule that every syllable has a vowel sound to count the syllables in a printed word (RF.1.3d), and decode two-syllable words by breaking them into syllables (RF.1.3e, which completes RF.1.3): closed VC/CV (magnet, picnic), compound words (sunset), open plus closed (moment, open), CVCe in a second syllable (cupcake, sunshine), and by year's end the vowel-team and r-controlled syllables (raincoat, garden). Introduces syllable-types: closed, open, silent e, vowel team, r-controlled, each recognized by its vowels. Order follows the base text's grade 1 modules 3 and 4. Grows from kindergarten's spoken syllables (ek-early-phonology) to printed ones. Boundary: two syllables; longer words wait for grade 2 and 3.

words: ending; -s; -es; -ed; -ing; -er; -est; base word
notes: Read words with inflectional endings (RF.1.3f): -s and -es as plurals and as action endings (foxes, fishes), -ing, -ed in its three sounds (/t/ jumped, /d/ yelled, /id/ melted), -er and -est (harder, hardest), and the rule for dropping silent e before a vowel suffix (bake, baking). Order follows the base text's grade 1 cycles, where each ending is added as the base words it fits are taught. Practised in decodable text and dictation. Grows from kindergarten, where endings were heard as clues to meaning (ek-unknown-words, word-parts), to reading and spelling them. Boundary: doubling the final consonant (running) is grade 2.

words: said; was; were; could; would; because; does; their; there; who
notes: Recognize and read grade 1 irregularly spelled words (RF.1.3g), taught a few a cycle by mapping: tap the sounds, mark the regular letters and the part to learn by heart, read in a sentence, spell from memory. Question words and the days of the week come in their own cycles, as in the base text. Practised in decodable texts, sentence dictation and the class word wall. Grows from kindergarten high-frequency words (ek-high-frequency) toward words whose irregular part is larger. Boundary: once a word's pattern is taught (my after -y), it is read as decodable, not as a sight word.

words: spell; pattern; print; letter; sound it out; dictation
notes: Print all upper- and lowercase letters (L.1.1a); spell words with common spelling patterns and frequent irregular words correctly (L.1.2d); and spell untaught words phonetically from phonemic awareness and spelling rules (L.1.2e). These sit on a foundational row because the base text teaches them in the Skills Block with phonics: every taught pattern is spelled in dictation the same week it is read. Grows from kindergarten's many letters printed and simple phonetic spelling (ek-letter-names, ek-cvc-decoding) to all letters and correct spelling of taught patterns. Boundary: untaught patterns are judged by a sound for every phoneme, not by correct spelling.

words: reread; smooth; expression; check; makes sense; fix
notes: Read grade 1 text with enough accuracy and fluency to understand it (RF.1.4): read with purpose and understanding (a), read aloud with accuracy, a natural rate and expression on repeated readings (b), and use context to confirm or self-correct a word already decoded, rereading as needed (c). RL.1.10 and RI.1.10 sit here because they name the same reading of grade 1 prose, poetry and informational text, with prompting and support. Texts: decodable texts in the Skills Block, and short grade 1 texts on the module topic (sun, moon and stars; birds), plus shared poems for repeated reading with a partner. Grows from kindergarten's group reading of emergent texts (ek-emergent-reader, ek-group-reading) to the child's own reading of connected text. Boundary: RF.1.4c is a check after decoding, never guessing a word from a picture or the first letter; no rate target or timer is shown to the child.

words: question; answer; detail; who; what; where; when; why; how; text
notes: Ask and answer questions about key details in a story (RL.1.1) and an informational text (RI.1.1), and about key details of a text read aloud or information presented orally or through media (SL.1.2). Texts: complex read-alouds well above decoding level on the grade 1 topic sets (tools and work; sun, moon and stars; birds' bodies; caring for birds), plus the student's own shorter texts. Grows from kindergarten by dropping 'with prompting and support': the child now asks questions unprompted and answers from the text. Boundary: answers name the page or sentence that shows it.

words: retell; key detail; lesson; message; learn
notes: Retell a story with key details and show understanding of its central message or lesson (RL.1.2). Practised on picture-book stories and a few short folktales, for example stories of characters who solve a problem by persevering (module 1, tools and work) or why the sun and moon live in the sky (module 2). Grows from kindergarten retelling with support (ek-retell) by adding the message: what the character learned and what we learn. Boundary: one main lesson, stated in a sentence; the retell is still in order with the story-map.

words: character; setting; event; describe; narrator; telling; illustration; detail
notes: Describe characters, setting and major events using key details (RL.1.3); use illustrations and details to do so (RL.1.7, the illustration half of the same description); and identify who is telling the story at points in the text, a narrator or a character (RL.1.6). Practised on picture-book read-alouds on each topic set, for example a kitten mistaking the moon for a bowl of milk and stories of characters who care for a bird. Grows from kindergarten's identifying (ek-story-elements, ek-pictures-and-words) to describing with evidence from words and pictures. Boundary: who is telling is a narrator or a character; first and third person are not named until later.

words: feeling word; sense word; see; hear; smell; taste; touch; poem
notes: Identify words and phrases in stories or poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses (RL.1.4). Introduces figurative-language in its first form: words chosen to make a reader feel or sense something, collected on a five-senses chart. Practised on short poems about the sun, moon and sky (module 2, where the class writes its own narrative poem) and on story read-alouds. Grows from kindergarten's shades of meaning and real-life word use (ek-word-relationships). Boundary: noticing and naming the words; grade 2 adds rhythm, rhyme, alliteration and repeated lines (RL.2.4).

words: story; information; fiction; nonfiction; teach; tell
notes: Explain the major differences between books that tell stories and books that give information, from wide reading of many kinds (RL.1.5). Practised all year by sorting the module's books and asking what each is for, for example a story and an information book both about the moon (module 2). Grows from kindergarten's naming storybooks and poems (ek-books-and-authors) to explaining differences in purpose, structure and features. The base text treats it as integrated throughout. Boundary: the two big kinds only; genres within them come later.

words: compare; contrast; same; different; both; but
notes: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in stories (RL.1.9), and basic similarities and differences between two texts on the same topic (RI.1.9). One compare routine on two kinds of text. Practised on two true stories of rescued birds (module 4, assessed in the base text) and two informational texts on birds. Grows from kindergarten by dropping 'with prompting and support' (ek-compare-two). Boundary: two texts at a time, compared on details the child can point to.

words: main topic; key detail; retell; about
notes: Identify the main topic and retell key details of an informational text (RI.1.2). Practised on informational read-alouds and short texts on tools and work, the sun, moon and stars, and birds' bodies, using main-idea-details. Grows from kindergarten by dropping 'with prompting and support' (ek-main-topic). Boundary: one topic per text; grade 2 adds multiparagraph text and the focus of each paragraph (RI.2.2).

words: connect; because; so; pattern; first; then; same as
cross_subject: science:1-ESS1-1 (patterns of the sun, moon and stars read and observed)
notes: Describe the connection between two people, events, ideas or pieces of information in a text (RI.1.3): how a bird's beak connects to what it eats, why the sun seems to move across the sky. Practised on informational texts on birds' bodies and sky patterns. Grows from kindergarten by dropping 'with prompting and support' (ek-connections). Boundary: two linked pieces at a time; grade 2 asks for a series (RI.2.3).

words: context; clue; sentence; root word; ending; meaning
notes: Ask and answer questions to work out the meaning of words and phrases in an informational text (RI.1.4), choosing among strategies (L.1.4): the sentence around the word (L.1.4a), a common affix (L.1.4b), a root word and its inflected forms (look, looks, looked, looking) (L.1.4c). Introduces context-clues: reread the sentence, find the words that explain the new word. Practised on words from the module texts (feathers, beak, tool, orbit), assessed in the base text on a text about why people need birds. Grows from kindergarten's asking about unknown words (ek-unknown-words) by adding context as a strategy and naming root words. Boundary: context helps meaning, not decoding; the word is read first.

words: heading; table of contents; glossary; label; caption; icon; menu
notes: Know and use text features (headings, table of contents, glossary, labels, electronic menus and icons) to find key facts (RI.1.5). Practised on informational books about birds (module 3, the research module) and on a simple Curio Class web page. Grows from kindergarten's cover, back cover and title page (ek-books-and-authors). Boundary: grade 2 adds captions, bold print, subheadings and index and asks for efficient use (RI.2.5).

words: picture; photograph; diagram; words; information; shows; tells
notes: Tell the information given by pictures and illustrations from the information given by the words (RI.1.6), and use illustrations and details to describe a text's key ideas (RI.1.7). Practised on informational texts with photographs and labelled drawings of birds and sky patterns, and in the scientific bird drawing of module 3. Grows from kindergarten's matching a picture to the words (ek-pictures-and-words). Boundary: the child says which facts came from the picture and which from the words.

words: point; reason; support; author
notes: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text (RI.1.8). Practised on short informational texts that argue a point, such as why birds are helpful to people and plants and a debate about a hawk's nest on a city building (module 4). Grows from kindergarten by dropping 'with prompting and support' (ek-author-reasons). Boundary: find the reasons; grade 2 describes how they support the point (RI.2.8).

words: opinion; reason; because; I think; in conclusion
cross_subject: social-studies:ss1-claim-reasons (claims with reasons in social studies writing)
notes: Write an opinion piece that names the topic or book, states an opinion, gives a reason and gives some sense of closure (W.1.1). Introduces paragraph-frame: opening sentence, a middle with the reason, a closing sentence, color-coded. Practised on the bird's nest debate (module 4, the base text's opinion unit) after reading the evidence. Grows from kindergarten's opinion with no reason (ek-opinion) by adding one reason and an ending. Boundary: one reason; several reasons and linking words are grade 2 (W.2.1).

words: topic; fact; teach; closing; paragraph
cross_subject: science:1-LS1-1 (how birds use body parts to survive)
notes: Write an informative piece that names a topic, gives some facts about it and gives some sense of closure (W.1.2): how a tool helps do a job (module 1), how beaks or feathers help birds survive (module 3, an informational paragraph from research). Uses paragraph-frame and main-idea-details. Grows from kindergarten's naming and some information (ek-inform) by asking for facts and an ending. Boundary: several facts on one topic; definitions and a concluding section are grade 2 (W.2.2).

words: first; next; then; after that; finally; detail; ending
notes: Write a narrative that recounts two or more events in order, with some details, time words (first, next, then, finally) and some sense of closure (W.1.3). Practised in the narrative poem about what the sun sees, after the sky read-alouds and observations (module 2). Grows from kindergarten's loosely linked events with drawing (ek-narrate) by asking for sequence, time words and closure. Boundary: grade 2 adds a well-elaborated event and thoughts and feelings (W.2.3).

words: focus; feedback; kind; specific; helpful; revise; add; publish
notes: With adult help, focus on a topic, respond to peers' questions and suggestions, and add details (W.1.5); use digital tools to produce and publish writing, with peers (W.1.6). Peer critique is a taught protocol: kind, specific, helpful. Practised in revising the sun narrative poem (module 2) and the bird riddle cards and window bird portrait (modules 3 and 4). Grows from kindergarten by adding focus on a topic (ek-revise-publish). Teacher note: a class without devices publishes on paper; no child accounts, and no child's name or photograph posted outside the class.

words: research; question; notes; source; expert; observe
cross_subject: science:1-LS1-1 (shared research on bird body parts)
notes: Take part in shared research and writing projects, such as reading several how-to books and writing instructions (W.1.7), and, with help, recall information from experience or gather it from provided sources to answer a question (W.1.8). Practised in the sky notebook (module 2) and the whole-class then small-group research on birds' beaks and feathers (module 3). Grows from kindergarten's same wording by asking for notes in words and a product written from more than one source. Boundary: sources are provided; grade 2 removes 'with guidance and support' from W.2.8.

words: listen with care; one at a time; build on; I agree; I want to add; clarify
notes: Collaborative conversations about grade 1 topics and texts: follow agreed rules, listening with care and speaking one at a time (SL.1.1a), build on others' talk through several exchanges (SL.1.1b), and ask questions to clear up confusion (SL.1.1c); ask and answer questions about what a speaker says to gather information or clarify (SL.1.3). Practised in science talks about sky patterns (module 2) and small-group talk about illustrations (module 3). Grows from kindergarten's continuing a conversation (ek-discussion) to building on another's comment. Boundary: frames fade across the year; grade 2 links comments to others' remarks (SL.2.1b).

words: describe; detail; clearly; drawing; complete sentence
notes: Describe people, places, things and events with relevant details, saying ideas and feelings clearly (SL.1.4); add drawings or visuals to clarify (SL.1.5); and speak in complete sentences when the task calls for it (SL.1.6). Practised in sharing a classroom 'magnificent thing' the class built (module 1), describing sky observations (module 2) and explaining a bird drawing (module 3). Grows from kindergarten's describing with prompting (ek-describe-aloud) by asking for relevant details and complete sentences. Boundary: short prepared talk to a partner or small group.

words: noun; proper noun; pronoun; verb; past; present; future; adjective; and; but; or; so; because
notes: Grammar in speaking and writing (L.1.1, completed here with L.1.1a on e1-spell-and-print and L.1.1j on e1-sentences): common, proper and possessive nouns (b); nouns matched with verbs (he hops, we hop) (c); personal, possessive and indefinite pronouns (d); verbs for past, present and future (e); common adjectives (f), conjunctions (g), determiners (h) and prepositions (i). Taught in short daily language work using sentences from the module texts and the child's drafts, then checked in writing (the base text assesses these in the performance tasks and the opinion unit). Grows from kindergarten's oral nouns, verbs, plurals and prepositions (ek-grammar-in-talk). Boundary: used correctly, named simply; irregular plurals and verbs are grade 2.

words: statement; question; command; exclamation; and; comma; date; name
notes: Produce and expand complete simple and compound sentences of four kinds, statements, questions, commands and exclamations, in response to prompts (L.1.1j); capitalize dates and names (L.1.2a); use end punctuation (L.1.2b) and commas in dates and in a series of single words (L.1.2c); L.1.2 is completed here with the spelling parts on e1-spell-and-print. Sentence-combining grows from expanding to joining with and, but, so. Practised in interactive writing and editing on the module topics and in the sun narrative poems. Grows from kindergarten's shared expansion of a simple sentence (ek-sentences). Boundary: compound sentences with common conjunctions only.

words: category; kind of; is a; cozy; peek; glance; stare; large; gigantic; because
notes: With adult help, show understanding of word relationships and nuance (L.1.5): sort words into categories (a), define a word by category and an attribute (a duck is a bird that swims) (b), find real-life connections (places at home that are cozy) (c), and tell shades of meaning among verbs that differ in manner (look, peek, glance, stare) and adjectives that differ in intensity (large, gigantic) (d). Use words learned from texts and talk, including conjunctions such as because for simple relationships (L.1.6). Practised on each module's word list from its texts (bird words, sky words). Grows from kindergarten's sorting objects and acting out verbs (ek-word-relationships) to sorting words and defining. Boundary: oral and written; no dictionary yet.

words: long vowel; short vowel; vowel team; oi; oy; ou; ow; oo; ew; aw; au
notes: Tell long from short vowels when reading regularly spelled one-syllable words (RF.2.3a), reviewing each long vowel and its spellings in turn (a: ai, ay; e: ee, ea, y; i: igh, ie; o: oa, ow), and know the spellings of additional vowel teams (RF.2.3b): oi, oy, ou, ow, then oo, ou, ui, ue, ew (decoding first), then aw, au. Order follows the base text's grade 2 modules 1 to 3. Practised in decodable and engagement texts, word sorts and dictation. Grows from grade 1's common vowel teams (e1-long-vowels) and long against short vowel sounds heard (e1-phonemes). Boundary: one-syllable words for new teams; two-syllable use is e2-two-syllable-words.

words: syllable; open; closed; consonant-le; r-controlled; long vowel; split
notes: Decode regularly spelled two-syllable words with long vowels (RF.2.3c): a review of r-controlled, open and closed syllables, then the consonant-le syllable (table, puzzle), with each syllable type spotted by its vowels. The base text adds -cle and -cal, -ous and -us as late endings. Practised in syllable-by-syllable reading of words from decodable texts and from the module's science texts (fossil, pollen). Grows from grade 1's two-syllable words with the first syllable types (e1-syllables). Boundary: two syllables; three-syllable words and the schwa in longer words carry into grade 3.

words: prefix; suffix; base word; -ed; -ing; -tion; -sion; -able; -ible; dis-; un-; re-
notes: Decode words with common prefixes and suffixes (RF.2.3d): doubling the consonant before a suffix (rub, rubbing), the three sounds of -ed, -tion and -sion, -able and -ible, the -y to -ies plural, then the prefixes dis-, de-, im-, in-. Order follows the base text's grade 2 modules 2 to 4. The meaning side of the same affixes is e2-word-strategies (L.2.4b). Grows from grade 1's inflectional endings (e1-inflections). Boundary: one prefix or suffix on a known base word; Latin and Greek roots begin in grade 3.

words: tricky; pattern; c; k; ck; ge; dge; ch; tch; old; ind; schwa
notes: Identify words with inconsistent but common spelling-sound patterns (RF.2.3e): old, ost, ind, ild (long vowel in a closed-looking word); c, k and ck; ge and dge; ch and tch; schwa spelled a, e and o; -ate said two ways. Recognize and read grade 2 irregularly spelled words (RF.2.3f), taught by mapping as in grade 1. Completes RF.2.3. Order follows the base text's grade 2 modules 2 to 4. Grows from grade 1 irregular words (e1-irregular-words). Boundary: the generalizations are stated as 'usually', with the common exceptions listed, never as guesses.

words: pattern; spell; check; dictionary; alphabetical order; guide word
notes: Generalize learned spelling patterns when writing words (cage to badge, boy to boil) (L.2.2d), and use reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, to check and correct spelling (L.2.2e). L.2.2 is completed here with the capital, comma and apostrophe parts on e2-sentences. Taught with the Skills Block patterns, as in the base text: each week's pattern is spelled in dictation, then found in the child's own drafts at the editing step. Grows from grade 1's correct spelling of taught patterns and phonetic spelling of untaught ones (e1-spell-and-print). Boundary: beginning dictionaries only; spell-checkers are not the check.

words: reread; phrase; expression; accuracy; check; makes sense
notes: Read grade 2 text with enough accuracy and fluency to understand it (RF.2.4: purpose and understanding, accuracy, rate and expression on repeated reads, context to confirm or self-correct), and by the end of the year read and understand literature (RL.2.10) and informational texts in history, science and technical subjects (RI.2.10) in the grades 2 to 3 band (about 420 to 820 Lexile), with scaffolding at the high end. The base text moves the reading demand here: in modules 1 and 2 complex text is still heard aloud, in modules 3 and 4 students read complex text in the band with more independence. Texts: decodable and engagement texts, and Curio Class's own grade 2 texts on schools, fossils and pollinators. Grows from grade 1's reading with prompting and support (e1-fluency). Boundary: no rate target or timer shown to the child; the teacher holds any watch.

words: who; what; where; when; why; how; key detail; evidence; recount
notes: Ask and answer who, what, where, when, why and how questions to show understanding of key details in a story (RL.2.1) and an informational text (RI.2.1), and recount or describe key ideas from a text read aloud or presented orally or through media (SL.2.2). Practised on the grade 2 topic sets (schools and community around the world; fossils and a famous fossil hunter; plants and pollination; protecting pollinators) in read-alouds and in the child's own reading; the base text introduces selected-response questions with this skill in module 2. Grows from grade 1's key-detail questions (e1-key-details) to the full set of question words with why and how answered from the text. Boundary: answers cite a page, a sentence or a picture caption.

words: fable; folktale; moral; lesson; message; culture; recount
cross_subject: social-studies:ss2-culture-migration (stories as part of a culture)
notes: Recount stories, including fables and folktales from diverse cultures, and determine their central message, lesson or moral (RL.2.2). Practised on short fables and folktales featuring animal characters, including pollinators, from several cultures (module 4), and on module 2 stories. Grows from grade 1's retelling with a lesson (e1-retell-lesson) to the fable and folktale as kinds, and to a stated moral across cultures. Teacher note: folktales from a living culture are chosen with care, credited to the culture they come from, and told without mocking accents or costumes. Boundary: stated in one sentence with the story's evidence.

words: character; respond; challenge; event; feel; act
notes: Describe how characters in a story respond to major events and challenges (RL.2.3). Practised on chapter-length and picture-book stories about school life and belonging (module 1, a story about a child who feels unseen at school) and stories of discovery (module 2). Grows from grade 1's describing characters (e1-characters) to explaining a character's response to an event. Teacher note: stories about a child left out at school may stir feelings; the teacher keeps talk on the character and offers a private way to share. Boundary: response to an event, shown by actions and words in the text.

words: rhythm; beat; rhyme; alliteration; repeated line; poem; song
notes: Describe how words and phrases (regular beats, alliteration, rhymes, repeated lines) supply rhythm and meaning in a story, poem or song (RL.2.4). Practised on short poems and songs on the module topics and on read-aloud stories with refrains. Figurative-language grows from grade 1's feeling and sense words (e1-feeling-sense-words) to sound devices that carry meaning. Boundary: notice and describe effect; similes and metaphors are named in grade 3 and 4.

words: beginning; middle; ending; introduce; conclude; structure
notes: Describe the overall structure of a story, how the beginning introduces it and the ending concludes the action (RL.2.5). Practised on stories read in module 2 (fossil discovery stories) before the class writes its own narrative about discovering a fossil, so reading and writing narrative-arc meet. Grows from grade 1's ordered retelling (e1-retell-lesson) and written sequence of events (e1-narrative). Boundary: beginning and ending in detail; chapters and scenes are grade 3 (RL.3.5).

words: point of view; character; voice; dialogue; says; thinks
notes: Acknowledge differences in the points of view of characters, including by speaking in a different voice for each character when reading dialogue aloud (RL.2.6). Practised on stories with two or more characters who see an event differently, and in reader's theatre of a module story; the base text assesses it with a videobook of a story (module 4). Grows from grade 1's identifying who is telling (e1-characters). Boundary: characters' points of view; the reader's own point of view is grade 3 (RL.3.6).

words: illustration; diagram; image; character; setting; plot; clarify; shows how
notes: Use information from illustrations and words in a print or digital text to show understanding of characters, setting or plot (RL.2.7), and explain how specific images, such as a diagram showing how something works, add to and clarify an informational text (RI.2.7). Practised on illustrated stories about schools and fossils, and on diagrams of a flower's parts and the pollination cycle (module 3). Grows from grade 1's using illustrations to describe (e1-characters, e1-pictures-and-words) to explaining what an image adds. Boundary: the image is read with the words, never in place of them.

words: compare; contrast; version; author; culture; important point; both
cross_subject: social-studies:ss2-two-accounts (comparing two accounts of one event)
notes: Compare and contrast two or more versions of the same story, such as a tale told by different authors or from different cultures (RL.2.9), and the most important points of two texts on the same topic (RI.2.9). Practised on two versions of a folktale (module 4) and two informational texts on pollinators or fossils. Grows from grade 1's comparing characters and two texts on details (e1-compare-two) to comparing versions and the most important points. Boundary: two texts at a time, with a chart.

words: main topic; paragraph; focus; heading; detail
notes: Identify the main topic of a multiparagraph text and the focus of particular paragraphs in it (RI.2.2). Practised on informational texts of several paragraphs about schools around the world, fossils, and plants and pollinators. Grows from grade 1's main topic of a whole text (e1-main-topic) to the paragraph as a unit. Boundary: focus of a paragraph named in a phrase; main idea stated in a sentence is grade 3 (RI.3.2).

words: series; sequence; steps; cause; then; after; process; cycle
cross_subject: science:2-LS2-2 (the steps of pollination and seed dispersal)
notes: Describe the connection between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in a technical procedure in a text (RI.2.3): how a fossil forms over time, the steps by which a bee carries pollen, how a seed packet's instructions work. Text-structure grows to sequence and cause chains. Practised on informational texts in modules 2 to 4. Grows from grade 1's connection between two pieces (e1-connections) to a series. Boundary: chains of three to five steps; named text structures (problem-solution, compare) come in grade 3.

words: context; prefix; root word; compound word; glossary; dictionary; meaning
notes: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text on a grade 2 topic (RI.2.4), choosing among strategies (L.2.4): sentence context (a); a known prefix on a known word (happy, unhappy; tell, retell) (b); a known root (addition, additional) (c); the parts of a compound word (birdhouse, notebook) (d); glossaries and beginning dictionaries, print and digital (e). Practised on domain words from the module texts (paleontologist, fossil, pollen, nectar) and general academic words that recur. Grows from grade 1's context and root words (e1-word-strategies) by adding prefixes, compounds and reference tools. Boundary: one strategy chosen and checked by rereading the sentence.

words: caption; bold print; subheading; glossary; index; menu; icon; locate
notes: Know and use text features (captions, bold print, subheadings, glossaries, indexes, electronic menus, icons) to find key facts efficiently (RI.2.5). Practised on informational books and web pages about plants and pollinators (module 3, a research module) and fossils. Grows from grade 1's headings, table of contents and glossary (e1-text-features) by adding captions, bold print, subheadings and index, and asking for efficient use. Boundary: locate facts for a question; search-engine use is not taught.

words: purpose; answer; explain; describe; author wants
notes: Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author wants to answer, explain or describe (RI.2.6). Practised on informational texts in modules 2 and 3 (what does a paleontologist do; why do plants need pollinators). Grows from grade 1's knowing that books give information or tell stories (e1-stories-and-information) to the specific purpose of one text. Boundary: purpose stated from the text; author's point of view against the reader's is grade 3 (RI.3.6).

words: point; reason; support; evidence; explain
notes: Describe how reasons support specific points the author makes in a text (RI.2.8). Practised on short texts that argue for protecting pollinators and planting wildflowers (module 4, the base text's opinion unit). Grows from grade 1's identifying reasons (e1-author-reasons) to explaining how a reason supports a point. Boundary: reasons stated in the text; judging whether evidence is sufficient begins in grade 4.

words: opinion; reason; because; also; and; in conclusion; linking word
cross_subject: social-studies:ss2-claim-sources (a claim with reasons from a named source)
notes: Write an opinion piece that introduces the topic or book, states an opinion, gives reasons that support it, links them with words such as because, and, also, and ends with a concluding statement or section (W.2.1). Practised in module 4: an opinion about which wildflower to plant for pollinators, written on the seed packet after reading the evidence. Grows from grade 1's one reason (e1-opinion) to several reasons with linking words and a concluding statement. Boundary: reasons from the texts and observations; counterclaims are not in K to 5.

words: introduce; topic; fact; definition; point; conclusion; paragraph
cross_subject: science:2-LS2-1 (what plants need, written up from investigations)
notes: Write an informative piece that introduces a topic, uses facts and definitions to develop points, and ends with a concluding statement or section (W.2.2). Practised in an informational book on the most important thing about schools (module 1) and an informational paragraph on plants and pollinators drafted in two parts (module 3). Grows from grade 1's some facts and a sense of closure (e1-informative) by adding definitions, points developed with facts, and a concluding statement. Boundary: one or two paragraphs; grouping into sections with headings is grade 3 (W.3.2a).

words: event; detail; action; thought; feeling; then; later; finally; ending
notes: Write a narrative that recounts a well-elaborated event or a short sequence of events, with details of actions, thoughts and feelings, time words for order, and a sense of closure (W.2.3). Practised in an illustrated narrative about discovering a fossil (module 2), after reading true and imagined discovery stories. Grows from grade 1's two or more events with some details (e1-narrative) by elaborating one event with actions, thoughts and feelings. Boundary: dialogue is welcome but not required until grade 3 (W.3.3b).

words: focus; revise; edit; feedback; checklist; publish
notes: With help from adults and peers, focus on a topic and strengthen writing by revising and editing (W.2.5), and use digital tools to produce and publish writing, with peers (W.2.6). Revising uses peer critique and sentence work from the anchor texts (sentence-combining); editing uses a short checklist of taught conventions. Practised on every module's performance task. Grows from grade 1's adding details after feedback (e1-revise-publish) by naming revising and editing as two steps, with peers as well as adults. Teacher note: devices are not assumed; a paper route is planned, and no child's name, voice or photograph is posted outside the class.

words: research; report; observation; notes; source; question
notes: Take part in shared research and writing projects, such as reading several books on one topic to write a report or recording science observations (W.2.7), and recall or gather information from experiences or provided sources to answer a question (W.2.8, now without 'with guidance and support'). Practised in the plants and pollinators research and the class poster and talk (module 3) and fossil notes (module 2). Grows from grade 1's adult-guided gathering (e1-shared-research) to the child gathering from provided sources alone. Teacher note: outdoor observation of bees and other pollinators keeps a distance; ask families about bee-sting allergies first. Boundary: sources still provided; finding sources is grade 3 and later.

words: gain the floor; build on; link; clarify; explain more; I agree with ... because
cross_subject: social-studies:ss2-family-interviews (asking a speaker questions to gather information)
notes: Collaborative conversations about grade 2 topics and texts: gain the floor respectfully and speak one at a time (SL.2.1a), link one's comments to others' remarks (SL.2.1b), ask for clarification and further explanation (SL.2.1c); ask and answer questions about what a speaker says to clarify, gather information or deepen understanding (SL.2.3). Practised in small-group discussion protocols on school stories (module 1, assessed in the base text) and in presentations and questions at the end of each module. Grows from grade 1's building on others' talk (e1-discussion) to linking comments and asking for more explanation. Boundary: frames now mostly faded; the teacher still names the protocol.

words: tell; recount; detail; coherent; record; audio; formal; informal
notes: Tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate facts and descriptive details, speaking audibly in coherent sentences (SL.2.4); create audio recordings of stories or poems and add drawings to clarify (SL.2.5); speak in complete sentences that give requested detail or clarification (SL.2.6); compare formal and informal English (L.2.3a), here because the choice is practised when speaking to an audience. Practised in the oral presentation on plants and pollinators (module 3), a videobook of a story (module 4) and the reflection presentation at year's end. Grows from grade 1's describing with relevant detail (e1-describe-present) to a coherent spoken story and a recorded one. Teacher note: recordings stay in class; a child may present without being recorded.

words: collective noun; group; plural; feet; mice; myself; past tense; told; adjective; adverb
notes: Grammar in speaking and writing (L.2.1, completed here with L.2.1f on e2-sentences): collective nouns (a), irregular plurals (feet, children, mice, fish) (b), reflexive pronouns (myself, ourselves) (c), past tense of common irregular verbs (sat, hid, told) (d), and adjectives against adverbs, chosen by what is modified (e). Taught on sentences from the module texts and the child's drafts; the base text assesses irregular past tense in the fossil narrative. Grows from grade 1's nouns, pronouns, verb tenses and adjectives (e1-grammar) to the irregular forms. Boundary: forms used correctly in writing; abstract nouns and verb tenses beyond simple are grade 3.

words: expand; rearrange; compound; capital; holiday; comma; greeting; closing; apostrophe; contraction; possessive
notes: Produce, expand and rearrange simple and compound sentences (The boy watched the movie; The little boy watched the movie; The action movie was watched by the little boy) (L.2.1f); capitalize holidays, product names and places (L.2.2a); commas in letter greetings and closings (L.2.2b); apostrophes for contractions and common possessives (L.2.2c, taught in the Skills Block a contraction family a cycle: not, is, would, will, us). Sentence-combining grows from joining to rearranging. Practised in interactive editing and in letters written in the community modules. Grows from grade 1's four kinds of simple and compound sentences and commas in dates and series (e1-sentences). Boundary: the rearranged passive form is noticed, not named.

words: spicy; juicy; toss; throw; hurl; thin; slender; skinny; scrawny; describe
notes: Show understanding of word relationships and nuance (L.2.5, now without 'with guidance and support'): real-life connections between words and their use (foods that are spicy or juicy) (a), and shades of meaning among closely related verbs (toss, throw, hurl) and adjectives (thin, slender, skinny, scrawny) (b). Use words learned from texts and talk, including adjectives and adverbs to describe (L.2.6). Practised on the module word lists (fossil, pollinator and school words), with each word met before, during and after reading and used again in the next module. Grows from grade 1's categories and shades of meaning with adult help (e1-word-relationships). Boundary: no figurative meanings of words yet; L.3.5 brings literal and nonliteral.
